title: ACED-Bench: Evaluating How LLM Agents Acquire and Act on Causal Evidence
abstract: arXiv:2610.14381v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as scientific assistants, yet we still lack reliable ways to evaluate whether they can investigate a system rather than merely answer a prompt. A useful evaluation must let agents choose experiments, interpret finite evidence, and make causal decisions, while keeping the environment coherent across repeated observations and interventions and preserving objective ground truth. We introduce ACED-BENCH (Active Causal Evidence and Decision Benchmark), a neuro-symbolic benchmark built around this requirement. The key idea is to separate the readable scientific surface from the formal causal world: LLMs generate natural-language scenarios and task text, while hidden probabilistic graphical models define the causal graph, data-generating process, intervention semantics, validation checks, and oracle answers. translated_title: ACED-Bench：评估大语言模型智能体如何获取并利用因果证据
translated_abstract: 大语言模型正越来越多地被用作科学助手，但我们仍然缺乏可靠的方法来评估它们能否真正研究一个系统，而不仅仅是回答提示。一个有效的评估必须让智能体能够选择实验、解读有限的证据并做出因果决策，同时在重复观察和干预中保持环境的一致性，并保留客观的真实标准答案。我们提出了 ACED-BENCH（主动因果证据与决策基准），这是一个围绕上述需求构建的神经符号基准。其核心思想是将可读的科学表层与形式化的因果世界分离：由大语言模型生成自然语言场景和任务文本，而隐藏的概率图模型则定义因果图、数据生成过程、干预语义、验证检查以及标准答案。由此产生的科学世界对智能体而言自然且可探究，同时又足够精确……
tldr: 提出神经符号基准 ACED-Bench，通过将大语言模型生成的自然语言科学场景与隐藏概率图模型定义的因果结构和标准答案分离，系统评估智能体主动选择实验、解读有限证据并做出因果决策的能力。
en_tdlr: ACED-Bench is a neuro-symbolic benchmark that separates LLM-generated natural-language scientific scenarios from hidden probabilistic graphical models to evaluate whether LLM agents can actively choose experiments, interpret finite evidence, and make sound causal decisions.
